issue.title: tools/validate_sase_core_rs hardcodes agent-stats work-schema version 5, but linked sase-core HEAD ships 6
issue.description:
Reproduction in workspace sase_18 (host project gh_sase-org__sase) on 2026-08-17 while
verifying an unrelated, Python-only change (plan 202608/config_cache_atomic_publication.md,
bead sase-ns.6.6.6.1 -- touches only src/sase/config/core.py, tests/test_config_cache.py,
tests/test_config_cache_token.py, tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt; no Rust or schema
code). `just install` succeeds, but every gate that depends on the shared `_setup` Justfile
recipe (`just check`, `just check-full`, `just lint`, `just test-scoped`,
`just test-contention`, `just selection-health`) fails at `_setup`:

    [validate_sase_core_rs] agent statistics work-schema probe requires schema version 5: got 6
    error: recipe `_setup` failed on line 121 with exit code 1

`tools/validate_test_environment` reports the built `sase_core_rs` as stale (bit 2),
`_setup` rebuilds it from the linked checkout at sase/repos/linked/sase-core (currently
`02a37e9` "fix(agent_stats): correct commit, spec, runner, and xprompt counters", one
commit ahead of the `875309a` "chore: release v0.27.17 (#141)" tag), then
`tools/validate_sase_core_rs`'s `_validate_agent_stats_work_schema` probe
(tools/validate_sase_core_rs:497) calls `agent_stats_query_runs` on the freshly built
extension and asserts `payload["schema_version"] == 5`. The linked checkout's HEAD
commit bumped the real payload to schema_version 6, but the Python-side probe was never
updated to match, so any workspace that builds from that checkout (rather than
resolving `sase-core-rs` from the pinned `>=0.27.15,<0.28.0` PyPI window in
pyproject.toml/uv.lock) hits this hard failure regardless of what Python change is
being verified.

Root cause is precisely located: tools/validate_sase_core_rs:497 hardcodes
`payload.get("schema_version") != 5`. Fix is either (a) bump that literal to 6 once the
schema-6 payload shape is confirmed stable and reflected in the rest of the probe's
assertions (`work`, `xprompts`, `runners` fields further down in the same function), or
(b) this is really floor/version-skew debt of the same shape as closed tasks sase-lm,
sase-kx, sase-jj, sase-hz -- advance the sase-core-rs floor once a release containing
02a37e9 is cut, and treat the literal-5 check as needing to track the release, not the
linked dev checkout.

RELATED: sase-km (closed canceled) proposed a general floor gate that understands wire-
schema versions rather than just binding names/version numbers -- exactly the gate class
that would have caught this. Not reopening it (deprioritized in 2026-08-14 triage, not a
duplicate of this specific occurrence). sase-lm, sase-kx, sase-jj, sase-hz, sase-jw are
prior distinct occurrences of the same "linked sase-core checkout ahead of/behind sase's
pinned expectations" class, each filed and fixed as its own task per established
precedent; this is a new occurrence of that pattern for the agent-stats work-schema
specifically.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-km — closed/canceled proposal for a general floor gate that understands wire-schema versions; would have caught this class of skew.

payload.close_reason: Already fixed on master by epic phase sase-oo.1 (commit 24936ffee 'fix(core): require agent-stats schema 6 and truncation fields', part of the same schema-bump work that caused this). Independently authored the identical fix (tools/validate_sase_core_rs schema_version 5->6) in workspace sase_18 to unblock a commit whose pre-commit hook was failing on this, but sase_git_commit's rebase pulled in origin/master's already-landed, more complete version (which also seeds probe xprompt data and validates new commit-counter fields), superseding my local edit -- confirmed via 'git diff --stat' showing tools/validate_sase_core_rs no longer dirty after the commit/rebase. No action needed; recording for the record.

payload.description: closed/canceled proposal for a general floor gate that understands wire-schema versions; would have caught this class of skew.
